description: Grounded couples-therapy scenarios for comparing a minimax-tree engine against plain LLMs. Personality-type input is the IPIP-50 Big Five inventory (Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Emotional Stability) — not MBTI. Each partner's 'personality_type' block is the actual engine input: 5 domain scores on the standard IPIP-50 raw scale (10 items/domain, 1-5 each, so range 10-50; low 10-23, medium 24-36, high 37-50). Note: IPIP-50 scores Emotional Stability, not Neuroticism directly — high emotional_stability = low neuroticism/more stable. 'clinical_context' (attachment style, Gottman conflict style) is narrative grounding only, explaining why the scenario is realistic and what dynamic it's testing — it is NOT part of the engine's input schema, just documentation for scenario designers/raters. Each scenario gives a seed_dialogue ending right before the AI agent must respond. Feed the same personality_type profiles + seed_dialogue into every model/engine under test, collect the next-turn response, and score against gold_response_criteria / red_flags using eval_scoring_rubric.md.

scenarios.title: Anxious pursuit vs. avoidant withdrawal after a late night out
scenarios.framework_source: Attachment theory (Pietromonaco et al.); pursuer-distancer dynamic
scenarios.situation: Dev came home 90 minutes late from drinks with coworkers without texting. Maya has been anxious all evening.

seed_dialogue.speaker: Maya
seed_dialogue.text: You didn't even text me. Do you know how many times I checked my phone? I thought something happened to you.

seed_dialogue.speaker: Dev
seed_dialogue.text: I'm home now, I'm fine. Can we not do this tonight?

seed_dialogue.speaker: Maya
seed_dialogue.text: That's not an answer. Why do you always shut me out when I'm trying to tell you how I feel?

seed_dialogue.speaker: Dev
seed_dialogue.text: Because every time I walk in the door you're already upset. I just need a minute.

known_failure_modes: agent sides with Maya and frames Dev as 'shutting down communication' without addressing Dev's need for space
agent sides with Dev and tells Maya she's 'overreacting', invalidating a low-emotional-stability fear response
agent gives generic advice ('communicate better') without naming the pursue-withdraw cycle
agent misses that Dev's 'can we not do this tonight' is an early-stage withdrawal signal, not stonewalling yet
gold_response_criteria: names or implicitly addresses the cycle: pursuit intensifying withdrawal and vice versa, without blaming either partner's temperament
validates Maya's underlying fear (abandonment/safety) separately from the behavior (repeated questioning)
validates Dev's need for a short decompression window without endorsing total avoidance
proposes a concrete, bounded next step (e.g., a short check-in now + a fuller conversation at an agreed time) rather than forcing full resolution immediately
red_flags: taking a side
pathologizing either partner
generic 'you both need to communicate' with no structure
ignoring the personality_type scores entirely

scenarios.title: Volatile vs. conflict-avoiding mismatch over money
scenarios.situation: Priya discovered a $2,000 credit card charge Sam didn't mention. Priya wants to hash it out immediately; Sam wants to drop it.

seed_dialogue.speaker: Priya
seed_dialogue.text: We are talking about this right now, Sam. Two thousand dollars and you said nothing?

seed_dialogue.speaker: Sam
seed_dialogue.text: It's handled. I paid it off already. Can we just move on?

seed_dialogue.speaker: Priya
seed_dialogue.text: That is not the point! The point is you hid it from me. I want to actually talk through this, not sweep it under the rug like you always do.

seed_dialogue.speaker: Sam
seed_dialogue.text: There's nothing to talk through. I don't see why this has to become a whole thing.

known_failure_modes: agent frames Priya's directness/intensity as itself the problem ('you're being too aggressive'), misreading a stable volatile style as hostility
agent frames Sam's avoidance as pure evasiveness rather than a documented, valid-if-mismatched conflict style
agent tries to force a single 'right' amount of conflict engagement instead of negotiating a shared ritual both styles can tolerate
agent ignores the secrecy/trust breach and jumps straight to communication-style coaching
gold_response_criteria: distinguishes the trust/transparency issue (hidden charge) from the conflict-style mismatch (wants to engage vs. wants to disengage) and addresses both
offers a structure that respects both styles, e.g. a time-boxed discussion now with a defined end point
does not tell either partner their natural conflict style is wrong, only that the mismatch needs a negotiated process
red_flags: moralizing about the money itself
one-size-fits-all 'always fully engage' advice
dismissing Sam's avoidance as pathological

scenarios.title: Escalation toward physiological flooding
scenarios.situation: An argument about in-laws has escalated over 10 minutes; both partners are talking over each other with rising volume.

seed_dialogue.speaker: Jordan
seed_dialogue.text: Your mother has said that to me three times now and you just sit there and let her!

seed_dialogue.speaker: Alex
seed_dialogue.text: Oh here we go again, you bring this up every single time we see them, it's exhausting!

seed_dialogue.speaker: Jordan
seed_dialogue.text: Exhausting?! I'm exhausted defending myself to your entire family while you say NOTHING!

seed_dialogue.speaker: Alex
seed_dialogue.text: Maybe if you weren't so sensitive about everything I wouldn't have to constantly manage you around them!

known_failure_modes: agent continues trying to resolve the in-law content issue instead of recognizing escalating flooding
agent fails to flag the contempt-adjacent language ('so sensitive about everything', 'constantly manage you')
agent asks an open-ended question that invites further escalation instead of interrupting the cycle
agent doesn't propose a concrete break/self-soothing protocol
gold_response_criteria: recognizes rising physiological arousal cues (volume, interruption, absolutist language 'always/never/NOTHING') and interrupts the escalation rather than continuing content-level mediation
names the contempt-adjacent phrasing without shaming either speaker
proposes a concrete de-escalation step: a timed break (~20+ min) with an agreed return time, per Gottman protocol
does not attempt to resolve the in-law issue itself in this turn
red_flags: asking 'why do you feel that way' mid-flood
trying to adjudicate who's right about the in-laws
no de-escalation mechanism offered

scenarios.title: Two low-openness/low-extraversion partners, low-conflict but low-intimacy
scenarios.situation: Both partners agree things are 'fine' but a recent check-in survey shows both privately rated satisfaction low. Neither raises real issues unprompted.

seed_dialogue.speaker: Chris
seed_dialogue.text: I mean, we don't really fight, so I don't think there's a problem.

seed_dialogue.speaker: Robin
seed_dialogue.text: Yeah, things are pretty calm. I don't really have anything to add.

seed_dialogue.speaker: Chris
seed_dialogue.text: Right. I guess I don't know what we're supposed to talk about.

known_failure_modes: agent accepts 'things are fine' at face value and ends the session, missing the documented risk that low-openness/conflict-avoiding pairs under-report real issues
agent forces high-intensity emotional disclosure inappropriate for this pairing's style, causing shutdown
agent fails to use any low-pressure structured prompt to surface unspoken needs
gold_response_criteria: gently probes past the surface 'we're fine' using a low-pressure, structured, non-confrontational prompt (matches low-extraversion/avoidant style rather than fighting it)
normalizes that calm ≠ fully resolved for this pairing, without implying something is wrong with them
invites one small, low-stakes disclosure rather than demanding a full emotional inventory
red_flags: accepting 'fine' and moving on
high-pressure 'tell me how you really feel' demands
diagnosing the couple as broken

scenarios.title: High-stability, high-agreeableness control scenario
scenarios.situation: Minor disagreement about weekend plans; both partners are already handling it well.

seed_dialogue.speaker: Noah
seed_dialogue.text: I know you wanted a quiet weekend, but I already told my brother we'd visit. I should have checked with you first.

seed_dialogue.speaker: Elena
seed_dialogue.text: Yeah, I wish you'd asked, but I get it, family stuff comes up. Can we do a quiet Sunday instead to make up for it?

seed_dialogue.speaker: Noah
seed_dialogue.text: That works for me. Sorry again.

known_failure_modes: agent over-intervenes, injecting therapy-speak or unsolicited frameworks into a conversation that's already resolving well
agent manufactures a deeper conflict that isn't there
agent fails to recognize successful repair already in progress (Noah's ownership + Elena's compromise) and doesn't reinforce it
gold_response_criteria: minimal intervention — brief acknowledgment/reinforcement of the successful repair (ownership + compromise) rather than redirecting
does not introduce new conflict framing or diagnostic language
if it responds at all, keeps it short and affirming
red_flags: heavy therapeutic scaffolding for a non-problem
inventing unmet needs neither partner expressed
long response length disproportionate to the stakes

scenarios.title: Missed bid for connection mid-argument
scenarios.framework_source: Gottman bids for connection / turning toward-away-against
scenarios.situation: Mid-disagreement about chores, Tasha makes a small bid for connection (humor) that Ben misses by staying on-topic.

seed_dialogue.speaker: Tasha
seed_dialogue.text: I just feel like I'm doing all the dishes lately... also, remember when you tried to load the dishwasher like a Tetris champion and it all fell out? Ha.

seed_dialogue.speaker: Ben
seed_dialogue.text: Anyway, I think we should just split it by day of the week, that's simpler.

seed_dialogue.speaker: Tasha
seed_dialogue.text: ...sure, day of the week works I guess.

known_failure_modes: agent focuses only on the logistical chore-split content and never flags the missed bid
agent misreads Tasha's flattened 'sure, works I guess' as agreement rather than a minor disconnection signal
gold_response_criteria: notices the missed humor bid and Tasha's subsequent flattened tone as a turning-away moment
creates space for a brief repair (acknowledging the joke / reconnecting) before finalizing the logistics
still allows the practical chore-split conversation to proceed once the repair is made
red_flags: treating the exchange as purely logistical
not distinguishing genuine agreement from resigned/flattened agreement

scenarios.title: Criticism sliding into contempt
scenarios.framework_source: Gottman Four Horsemen — criticism and contempt
scenarios.situation: Discussion about Marcus forgetting an anniversary dinner reservation.

seed_dialogue.speaker: Lily
seed_dialogue.text: You forgot the reservation. Again. You never think about anyone but yourself.

seed_dialogue.speaker: Marcus
seed_dialogue.text: Wow, real mature. Guess I'm just the world's worst husband, huh?

seed_dialogue.speaker: Lily
seed_dialogue.text: Honestly? Sometimes I wonder why I even bother planning anything with someone this careless.

known_failure_modes: agent addresses only the surface content (the forgotten reservation) and misses the escalation from criticism ('you never') to contempt-adjacent language ('someone this careless', sarcastic tone in Marcus's reply)
agent fails to distinguish criticism (Lily's first line) from Marcus's sarcastic defensiveness from Lily's contemptuous escalation (third line)
agent doesn't offer the specific antidotes (gentle start-up, culture of appreciation) tied to each horseman
gold_response_criteria: identifies the specific horsemen present: criticism ('you never think about anyone but yourself'), sarcastic defensiveness (Marcus), and contempt-adjacent escalation (Lily's third line)
interrupts before further escalation, addressing the pattern rather than relitigating the missed reservation
offers a concrete reframe example (e.g., converting 'you never think about anyone but yourself' into a specific, behavior-focused statement)
red_flags: only discussing the reservation logistics
failing to name the contempt-adjacent language
generic 'let's all calm down' with no specific antidote

scenarios.title: Demand-withdraw specific to one partner's issue
scenarios.situation: Fatima wants to discuss Owen's lack of involvement in wedding planning (Fatima's issue); Owen typically engages fine on his own topics (e.g. finances) but withdraws here.

seed_dialogue.speaker: Fatima
seed_dialogue.text: I've sent you three vendor lists and you haven't looked at any of them. This is our wedding too.

seed_dialogue.speaker: Owen
seed_dialogue.text: I'll look at them eventually, I've just been busy.

seed_dialogue.speaker: Fatima
seed_dialogue.text: You always say that. I need you to actually engage with this, not just tell me you will.

seed_dialogue.speaker: Owen
seed_dialogue.text: Can we talk about this later? I really don't want to get into it right now.

known_failure_modes: agent treats this as a generic communication problem rather than the specific, well-documented topic-linked demand-withdraw pattern
agent assumes Owen withdraws across the board, when the scenario specifies it's specific to this topic
agent puts full responsibility on Owen to 'just engage more' without addressing why this particular topic triggers withdrawal
gold_response_criteria: recognizes the pattern as specific to Fatima's issue (wedding planning) rather than a global trait, per Christensen's topic-specific finding
explores what makes this topic specifically aversive for Owen (e.g., overwhelm, feeling judged) rather than assuming general avoidance
proposes a concrete small commitment (e.g., one vendor list, one sitting, time-boxed) rather than an open-ended 'engage more' ask
red_flags: framing Owen as a globally withdrawn/uninvolved partner
no concrete, bounded next step
putting all the behavior-change burden on one partner without addressing the topic-specific trigger
